releases.name: opencode-speak-tts 0.2.0 — summary tones and reading speed
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Named summary tones.** A long answer is condensed with a tone you choose in the summary view: **Default** (the full briefing), **Explain** (keeps the assistant's ideas), **Actions** (leads with what you have to do) and **Headlines** (the results as short sentences, like scanning).
- **Summary reading speed.** `0.5x` to `2x`, set from the `Speed` row in the summary view or from the speed label in the transport row while a summary plays. Changing it mid-read carries on from the same point instead of restarting the sentence.
- **The summary view always opens.** `☰ summary` / `/tts-summary` opens whether or not a summary exists, says which case it is, and lets you pick a tone and write one.

## Fixes

- Slower-than-normal speeds no longer fall back to SAPI. A negative rate is passed to Edge as one argument (`--rate=-50%`); as a separate token, argparse read `-50%` as an option and the request failed.
- A short answer honestly expanded into a longer summary is no longer rejected as an echo.
- `■` stops the whole read, not only the clip playing. A speed change no longer clears the control state out from under the read it handed over.
- The footer controls no longer shrink to nothing on a narrow terminal. The summary cache is keyed by tone and language, so switching tone re-summarises and switching back is free.

## Commands

`/tts-summary-rate` is new; `/tts-status` reports the tone and the speed.
